headline: From Practical NISQ Benchmarks to Uncloneable Encryption
summary: Today's papers bridge practical NISQ hardware evaluation with foundational quantum theory. Research highlights algorithmic advances like Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization alongside new cost and accuracy benchmarks. Concurrently, theoretical papers prove strict circuit complexity lower bounds, graph-driven quantum chaos, and secure uncloneable encryption.

themes.title: NISQ Simulation & Hardware Benchmarking
themes.body: Practical evaluations of current quantum hardware show distinct tradeoffs between cost, classical tensor network capabilities, and hybrid algorithm performance like Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization across physical systems.

themes.title: Quantum Complexity & Cryptographic Foundations
themes.body: Theoretical investigations establish strict lower bounds on local gate complexity, prove statistical uncloneable encryption for arbitrary message lengths, and demonstrate quantum chaos driven purely by network geometry.

connections.body: Both studies employ Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) to extend the reach of NISQ processors beyond standard VQE limits in physical and chemical simulations.
Both papers evaluate the practical limits of real quantum hardware, focusing on error thresholds versus classical DMRG benchmarks and cost-to-fidelity performance tradeoffs.
